# 1 Chronicles Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 375v–376r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_009_page_001.jpg, 1CH_009_page_002.jpg

---

**1** All Israel was registered in the genealogies recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel. The people of Judah were carried off to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.

**2** The first people to resettle in their former towns on their own property were ordinary Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.

**3** These people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem:

**4** Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani — a descendant of Perez son of Judah. **5** From the Shilonite clan: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons. **6** From the Zerahite clan: Jeuel and relatives — 690 people.

**7** From Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah; **8** Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah. **9** Their relatives, as listed in their genealogies, numbered 956. All were leaders of their clans.

**10** From the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin, **11** and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub — the chief official of God's temple. **12** Also Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer. **13** In all, there were 1,760 priests — capable men responsible for the service of God's house.

**14** From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, a Merarite; **15** Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph; **16** Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the Netophathite villages.

**17** The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman, with their relatives. Shallum was the chief. **18** Previously, he had been stationed at the king's gate on the east side. These men served as gatekeepers for the Levite camps.

**19** Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, along with his relatives from the Korahite clan, was responsible for guarding the entrance to the tent of worship — just as their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the LORD's camp. **20** Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their chief officer in earlier times, and the LORD was with him.

**21** Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

**22** In all, 212 men were chosen as gatekeepers. They were registered by genealogy in their home villages. David and Samuel the prophet had appointed them to this position of trust. **23** They and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the LORD's house — the tent-temple.

**24** Gatekeepers were stationed on all four sides — east, west, north, and south. **25** Their relatives in the villages took turns coming in for seven-day shifts. **26** The four chief gatekeepers, all Levites, were permanently on duty and were in charge of the storerooms and treasuries of God's house. **27** They spent the night stationed around God's house, because they were responsible for its security and for opening the doors each morning.

**28** Some gatekeepers were in charge of the equipment used in worship services — they counted every item when it went out and when it came back. **29** Others were responsible for the furnishings and sacred objects, as well as the supplies of fine flour, wine, olive oil, frankincense, and spices. **30** Some of the priests mixed the spiced anointing oils.

**31** Mattithiah, a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the ceremonial bread. **32** Some of their Kohathite relatives were in charge of preparing the showbread for every Sabbath.

**33** The musicians, all heads of Levite families, lived in rooms at the temple and were exempt from other duties because they were on call day and night.

**34** These were the heads of the Levite families, listed by their genealogies. They lived in Jerusalem.

**35** Jeiel, the founder of Gibeon, lived there with his wife Maacah. **36** His firstborn was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, **37** Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth. **38** Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

**39** Ner was the father of Kish; Kish the father of Saul; Saul the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal. **40** Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal's son was Micah.

**41** Micah's sons: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz. **42** Ahaz was the father of Jarah; Jarah the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza. **43** Moza was the father of Binea; then Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel.

**44** Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — "because of their unfaithfulness":** Nine chapters of genealogy end with a single devastating sentence. The word *ma'al* — treacherous unfaithfulness — appears here for the third time (after 2:7 and 5:25). The Chronicler has been building to this moment: the exile was not a tragedy that happened to Israel; it was the consequence of Israel's infidelity.

**Verses 2-34 — Who came back first:** This is a snapshot of the restored community — the people who first returned to rebuild. Four categories: ordinary Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants. The Chronicler wants the post-exilic community to see itself in this list: you are the continuation of the story.

**Verses 17-27 — The sacred gatekeepers:** These verses reveal an entire world of temple administration: rotating shifts, four-directional coverage, key custody, inventory control, supply management. The gatekeepers are not guards in a modern sense — they are Levites entrusted with the boundary between sacred and common space.

**Verse 22 — "David and Samuel":** An extraordinary claim: the gatekeeping system was established jointly by the king and the prophet. Two sources of authority — royal and prophetic — converge in the organization of worship.

**Verse 33 — Musicians "exempt from other duties":** The Hebrew *peturim* means "released, freed." Temple musicians were full-time worship leaders, not part-time volunteers. Their work of praise was considered so important that they were relieved of all other obligations. Day and night, the music never stopped.

**Verses 35-44 — Saul one more time:** The genealogy of Saul is repeated from chapter 8, creating a deliberate bridge. The genealogies began with Adam (1:1) and end with Saul — the king who failed. Chapter 10 will narrate his death. The Chronicler's message: Saul's line is recorded, but his story is a cautionary tale.

*— PNEUMA*
